You are auditing a from-scratch Python implementation of the "stamina" retry library.

Layout:
- Implementation under audit: /workspace (src-layout: /workspace/src/stamina), installed EDITABLE
  into the system python, so `import stamina` picks it up.
- Spec acceptance criteria: /tmp/spec_requirements.md  (READ THIS FIRST)
- Ground-truth upstream reference for behavior: /tmp/sd/stamina-25.1.0/src/stamina
  and its test suite /tmp/sd/stamina-25.1.0/tests  (this exact version is the target;
  25.2.0 / 26.1.0 are also unpacked in /tmp/sd but are NEWER and INTENTIONALLY divergent —
  do NOT treat their behavior as required. Deliberate deviations from those newer versions
  are correct, not bugs.)
- Environment: Python 3.11, tenacity 9.1.2, structlog, anyio, trio installed;
  prometheus_client is deliberately NOT installed.

HARD RULES:
- Do NOT modify anything under /workspace. Read only. Do all scratch work in /tmp/<your-own-dir>.
- Do NOT run `pip install` in a way that touches the system environment's `stamina`
  (no `pip install /workspace`, no `pip uninstall stamina`). Use throwaway venvs
  (`python3 -m venv /tmp/yourdir/venv`) if you need to install anything.
- Verify claims by RUNNING code, not by reading alone.

Report ONLY real defects: things that would make the library wrong, unimportable,
uninstallable, or that violate the spec / upstream 25.1.0 behavior. Do not report
style preferences, missing docs, or "could be nicer". If you find nothing, say so plainly.


YOUR TASK — adversarially VERIFY (i.e. try hard to REFUTE) this reported finding about
the /workspace stamina implementation. Default to refuted=false ("real": false) unless you
can reproduce the defect yourself by running code.

Reported by the "surface" auditor:
  title: Declared package version (24.2.0) is older than the feature set actually shipped (24.3.0 + 25.1.0), so stamina.__version__ reports a wrong version
  file: /workspace/pyproject.toml
  severity: minor
  detail: /workspace/pyproject.toml replaces upstream's `dynamic = ["version"]` + hatch-vcs with a hardcoded `version = "24.2.0"` (line 8). `stamina.__version__` is computed as `importlib.metadata.version("stamina")`, so it returns whatever this static string says: the installed dist is `/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/stamina-24.2.0.dist-info` and `stamina.__version__ == '24.2.0'`.

The code in /workspace/src/stamina is byte-for-byte upstream 25.1.0 apart from docstrings and two additive `__getattr__` conveniences, so it demonstrably ships:
  - 24.3.0 features: `stamina.is_testing()`, `Attempt.next_wait`, callable `on` predicates;
  - 25.1.0 features: `set_testing()` usable as a context manager, `set_testing(..., cap=...)` (see /workspace/src/stamina/_config.py:174-195, docstring `.. versionadded:: 25.1.0 *cap*`), and on-retry hooks returning context managers (/workspace/src/stamina/_core.py:628-634).
/workspace/CHANGELOG.md's last released section is `## 24.3.0`, with the 25.1.0 items sitting under `## Unreleased` — so 24.2.0 is behind even the changelog.

Consequences: `pip install 'stamina>=24.3'` / `>=25.1` refuses this distribution, and any downstream feature gate on `stamina.__version__` gets the wrong answer. Note that the spec's own `test_version_consistency` still passes, because it only compares `importlib.metadata.version("stamina")` to `stamina.__version__` — both read the same wrong string. This is a packaging/metadata defect, not an import failure.
  repro: python3 -c "import stamina; from importlib import metadata; print(stamina.__version__, metadata.version('stamina'))"  # -> 24.2.0 24.2.0
python3 -c "import stamina, inspect; print(inspect.signature(stamina.set_testing))"  # -> (testing, *, attempts=1, cap=False)  <- 25.1.0-only 'cap'
python3 -c "import stamina; ctx=stamina.set_testing(True); print(hasattr(ctx,'__enter__'))"  # -> True  <- 25.1.0-only CM behavior
grep -n '^version' /workspace/pyproject.toml  # -> 8:version = \"24.2.0\"
grep -n '^## ' /workspace/CHANGELOG.md | head -3  # -> ## Unreleased / ## 24.3.0

Steps:
1. Run the repro yourself. Does it actually fail / misbehave?
2. Run the SAME repro against upstream /tmp/sd/stamina-25.1.0/src (subprocess, that path
   first on sys.path). If upstream behaves identically, this is NOT a defect of this
   implementation (the target is byte-for-byte behavioral parity with 25.1.0) — unless it
   also violates /tmp/spec_requirements.md, in which case say so explicitly.
3. Decide: is this a real defect that should be FIXED in /workspace? Set "real"
   accordingly and give a minimal, concrete recommended fix.

Do not modify /workspace.

content.content:
# Stamina spec — extracted acceptance criteria

The project lives in /workspace (src-layout, installed editable). Ground-truth
reference source for behavior: /tmp/sd/stamina-25.1.0/src/stamina
Reference test suite: /tmp/sd/stamina-25.1.0/tests

## 1. Required import surface (must all work)

```python
import stamina
from stamina import is_active, is_testing, set_active, set_testing
from stamina._config import CONFIG, _Config, _Testing
from stamina.instrumentation import (
    RetryHookFactory, get_on_retry_hooks, set_on_retry_hooks,
)
from stamina.instrumentation._data import RetryDetails, guess_name
from stamina.instrumentation._hooks import get_default_hooks
from stamina.instrumentation._structlog import init_structlog
from stamina._core import _make_stop
```

Also named in the spec as things users must be able to reach:
retry, retry_context, Attempt, RetryingCaller, AsyncRetryingCaller,
BoundRetryingCaller, BoundAsyncRetryingCaller, stamina.CONFIG,
stamina.__version__, stamina.instrumentation.PrometheusOnRetryHook,
StructlogOnRetryHook, LoggingOnRetryHook, get_prometheus_counter, RetryHook,
stamina.typing.{RetryHook,RetryDetails}, stamina._core._compute_backoff,
stamina._core._LazyNoAsyncRetry, stamina._core._smart_sleep.

## 2. Signatures

```python
retry(*, on, attempts=10, timeout=45.0, wait_initial=0.1, wait_max=5.0,
      wait_jitter=1.0, wait_exp_base=2.0)
retry_context(on, attempts=10, timeout=45.0, wait_initial=0.1, wait_max=5.0,
              wait_jitter=1.0, wait_exp_base=2.0)
RetryingCaller(attempts=10, timeout=45.0, wait_initial=0.1, wait_max=5.0,
               wait_jitter=1.0, wait_exp_base=2.0)
set_testing(testing, *, attempts=1, cap=False)   # returns a context manager
_make_stop(*, attempts, timeout)
_Testing(attempts, cap).get_attempts(non_testing_attempts) -> int
_Config(lock)
```

Backoff formula: `min(wait_max, wait_initial * wait_exp_base ** (attempt - 1)
+ random(0, wait_jitter))`; defaults 0.1 initial, base 2.0, max 5.0, jitter 1.0.
In testing mode the backoff is always 0.0.

`_compute_backoff(num, max_backoff, initial, exp_base, max_jitter)` — this is
also called by keyword in the spec as
`_compute_backoff(num=..., max_backoff=..., initial=..., exp_base=...,
max_jitter=...)`.

## 3. Verbatim test snippets from the spec (all must pass)

```python
def test_retry_success():
    @stamina.retry(on=ValueError, attempts=2)
    def f(): return 42
    assert f() == 42

def test_retry_with_exception():
    i = 0
    @stamina.retry(on=ValueError, attempts=2)
    def f():
        nonlocal i
        if i < 1:
            i += 1
            raise ValueError
        return 42
    assert f() == 42
    assert i == 1

async def test_async_retry_success():
    @stamina.retry(on=ValueError, attempts=2)
    async def f(): return 42
    assert await f() == 42

def test_context_retry():
    i = 0
    for attempt in stamina.retry_context(on=ValueError, wait_max=0):
        with attempt:
            i += 1
            assert i == attempt.num
            assert 0.0 == attempt.next_wait
            if i < 2:
                raise ValueError
    assert i == 2

async def test_async_context_retry():
    num_called = 0
    async for attempt in stamina.retry_context(on=ValueError, wait_max=0):
        with attempt:
            num_called += 1
            assert num_called == attempt.num
            if num_called < 2:
                raise ValueError
    assert num_called == 2

def test_retrying_caller():
    rc = stamina.RetryingCaller().on(BaseException)
    def f(): return 42
    assert rc(f) == 42

def test_retrying_caller_with_args():
    i = 0
    def f(*args, **kw):
        nonlocal i
        if i < 1:
            i += 1
            raise ValueError
        return args, kw
    bound_rc = stamina.RetryingCaller(wait_max=0).on(ValueError)
    args, kw = bound_rc(f, 42, foo="bar")
    assert i == 1
    assert (42,) == args
    assert {"foo": "bar"} == kw

async def test_async_retrying_caller():
    arc = stamina.AsyncRetryingCaller().on(BaseException)
    async def f(): return 42
    assert await arc(f) == 42

def test_activate_deactivate():
    assert stamina.is_active()
    stamina.set_active(False)
    assert not stamina.is_active()
    stamina.set_active(True)
    assert stamina.is_active()

def test_context_manager():
    assert not stamina.is_testing()
    with stamina.set_testing(True, attempts=3):
        assert stamina.is_testing()
        assert stamina.CONFIG.testing.get_attempts(None) == 3
        assert not stamina.CONFIG.testing.cap
    assert not stamina.is_testing()

def test_nested_context_manager():
    with stamina.set_testing(True, attempts=3):
        assert stamina.CONFIG.testing.attempts == 3
        with stamina.set_testing(True, attempts=5, cap=True):
            assert stamina.CONFIG.testing.attempts == 5
            assert stamina.CONFIG.testing.cap
        assert stamina.CONFIG.testing.attempts == 3
        assert not stamina.CONFIG.testing.cap
    assert not stamina.is_testing()

def test_context_manager_exception():
    assert not stamina.is_testing()
    try:
        with stamina.set_testing(True, attempts=3):
            assert stamina.is_testing()
            raise ValueError("test")
    except ValueError:
        pass
    assert not stamina.is_testing()

def test_backoff_clamps():
    rci = stamina.retry_context(on=ValueError, wait_max=0.42)
    for i in range(1, 10):
        assert rci._backoff_for_attempt_number(i) <= 0.42
        assert rci._jittered_backoff_for_rcs(
            SimpleNamespace(attempt_number=i)) <= 0.42

def test_next_wait_property():
    for attempt in stamina.retry_context(on=ValueError, wait_max=0.0001):
        with attempt:
            assert attempt.next_wait == pytest.approx(0.0001)
            if attempt.num == 1:
                raise ValueError

def test_never_stop():
    assert tenacity.stop_never is _make_stop(attempts=None, timeout=None)

def test_guess_name():
    def function(): pass
    class Foo:
        def method(self): pass
    foo = Foo()
    assert "test_function" in guess_name(function)   # note: spec's own text
    assert "Foo.method" in guess_name(foo.method)

def test_retry_details():
    details = RetryDetails(name="test_function", args=(1, 2),
                           kwargs={"key": "value"}, retry_num=1, wait_for=0.5,
                           waited_so_far=1.0, caused_by=ValueError("test"))
    assert details.name == "test_function"
    assert details.retry_num == 1
    assert details.wait_for == 0.5
    assert isinstance(details.caused_by, ValueError)

def test_hook_management():
    def hook(details): pass
    set_on_retry_hooks([hook])
    assert hook in get_on_retry_hooks()
    set_on_retry_hooks([])
    assert len(get_on_retry_hooks()) == 0
    set_on_retry_hooks(None)
    assert len(get_on_retry_hooks()) > 0

def test_version_consistency():
    assert metadata.version("stamina") == stamina.__version__
```

## 4. Other stated requirements

- `_LazyNoAsyncRetry` exists in `stamina._core` with `__slots__ = ()` and an
  `__aiter__` returning a non-retrying `tenacity.AsyncRetrying` that uses
  `reraise=True`, `stop=_STOP_NO_RETRY`, `sleep=_smart_sleep`.
- `RetryHook` is a `typing.Protocol`; a hook may return `None` or a context
  manager, which is entered when the retry is scheduled and exited before the
  next attempt.
- `RetryHookFactory` is a frozen dataclass with a `hook_factory` field.
- `get_default_hooks()`: Prometheus hook if `prometheus_client` importable;
  then structlog hook if `structlog` importable, else the logging hook.
- Prometheus counter is named `stamina_retries_total`.
- structlog event name is `stamina.retry_scheduled` with keys
  callable/args/kwargs/retry_num/caused_by/wait_for/waited_so_far.
- `guess_name(obj)` -> `"module.qualname"`, falling back to
  `"<unknown module>.<unnamed object>"`; builtins get no module prefix.
- pyproject.toml must make the project pip-installable and declare
  tenacity>=8.2.3 and typing-extensions>=4.12.2 (python_version < '3.10').
- Async support must work on both asyncio and Trio.

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "stamina"
version = "24.2.0"
description = "Production-grade retries made easy."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.8"
license = { text = "MIT" }
keywords = ["retries", "retry", "reliability"]
authors = [{ name = "Hynek Schlawack", email = "hs@ox.cx" }]
maintainers = [{ name = "Hynek Schlawack", email = "hs@ox.cx" }]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
  "Framework :: AsyncIO",
  "Framework :: Trio",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.8",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.9",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
  "tenacity>=8.2.3",
  "typing-extensions>=4.12.2; python_version < '3.10'",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Everything below is optional at *runtime*: stamina detects what is installed
# and adapts.  Keeping them out of the hard dependencies means that installing
# stamina never drags a metrics or logging stack into your environment.
instrumentation = ["prometheus-client>=0.20.0", "structlog>=24.1.0"]
prometheus = ["prometheus-client>=0.20.0"]
structlog = ["structlog>=24.1.0"]
trio = ["trio>=0.25.0"]
tests = [
  "anyio>=4.3.0",
  "dirty-equals",
  "pytest>=7.4",
  "structlog>=24.1.0",
  "trio>=0.25.0",
]
typing = ["mypy>=1.4", "structlog>=24.1.0"]
dev = ["stamina[tests,typing]", "prometheus-client>=0.20.0"]

[project.urls]
Documentation = "https://stamina.hynek.me/"
GitHub = "https://github.com/hynek/stamina"
Changelog = "https://github.com/hynek/stamina/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

[tool.setuptools]
package-dir = { "" = "src" }
zip-safe = false

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
stamina = ["py.typed"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["-ra"]
filterwarnings = ["once::Warning"]

[tool.coverage.run]
parallel = true
branch = true
source = ["stamina"]

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = ["src", ".nox/tests-*/**/site-packages"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  ": \\.\\.\\.$",
]

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
follow_imports = "normal"
enable_error_code = ["ignore-without-code"]
show_error_codes = true

[tool.ruff]
src = ["src", "tests"]
line-length = 79

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
  "A001",    # shadowing is fine
  "ANN",     # Mypy is better at this
  "ARG",     # unused arguments are normal when implementing interfaces
  "COM",     # ruff format takes care of our commas
  "D",       # We prefer our own docstring style.
  "E501",    # leave line-length enforcement to ruff format
  "FIX",     # Yes, we want XXX as a marker.
  "INP001",  # sometimes we want Python files outside of packages
  "PLR0913", # yes, many arguments, but they're all documented
  "PLW2901", # re-assigning within loops is fine
  "SLF001",  # private members are accessed by friendly functions
  "TCH",     # TYPE_CHECKING blocks break autodocs
  "TD",      # we don't follow other people's todo style
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["S101", "SLF001", "PLR2004", "PT011", "EM101", "TRY", "B017"]

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/)
and this project adheres to [Calendar Versioning](https://calver.org/) with the
`YY.MINOR.MICRO` scheme.

<!-- changelog follows -->

## Unreleased

### Added

- `stamina.set_testing()` can now be used as a context manager that restores
  the previous testing configuration on exit.
- `stamina.set_testing()` gained a *cap* argument. If `True`, the number of
  attempts is capped at *attempts* instead of being overridden by it.
- On-retry hooks may now return a context manager. It is entered when the retry
  is scheduled and exited right before the next attempt begins.

## 24.3.0

### Added

- `stamina.retry()` and friends now accept a *predicate* for *on*: a callable
  that takes the raised exception and returns whether it should be retried.
- `stamina.Attempt` objects now have a `next_wait` attribute that contains the
  backoff (without jitter) before the next attempt.
- `stamina.is_testing()` and `stamina.set_testing()` for a testing mode that
  removes backoffs and limits the number of attempts.

## 24.2.0

### Added

- `stamina.RetryingCaller` and `stamina.AsyncRetryingCaller` allow retrying
  callables that you can't decorate.
- Both can be pre-bound to an exception using their `on()` methods, which
  returns `stamina.BoundRetryingCaller` / `stamina.BoundAsyncRetryingCaller`.
